takeaway: Endothelial cells make thrombomodulin, which binds thrombin and activates protein C; only the cerebral microcirculation lacks it.

question.text: The endothelial cells in all of the following circulations produce thrombomodulin except which one?

lines.text: Endothelial cells line our vessels, and each one carries a little shield: thrombomodulin.
When thrombin, the clotting villain, comes along, the shield grabs it and handcuffs it.
That slows the clotting, and it also switches on protein C, our policeman.
Activated protein C inactivates factors V and VIII, so the clot cannot keep growing.
lines.say: Activated protein C inactivates factors five and eight, so the clot cannot keep growing.

lines.text: Liver, skin, kidney and lung vessels all make thrombomodulin, so they all get a tick.
But the cerebral microcirculation is the odd one out: no thrombomodulin there.
lines.say: (laugh) But the cerebral microcirculation is the odd one out: no thrombomodulin there.

lines.text: So the answer is cerebral microcirculation.
